# Qnet 2.0 parity ledger

This ledger is the instrument that proves Qnet 2.0 keeps all the functionality of Qnet 0.90.34, as PLAN.md §5 requires. It has one row per thing the old app does: every menu item and shortcut, every toolbar item, canvas tool and gesture, inspector field, setting key with its default and range, method with its arguments, exporter, parser rule, file read or written, diagnostic, and every do-not-regress invariant. Each row names where the behaviour lives in the Swift source and the phase of PLAN.md §7 that ports it. A phase closes only when its rows are Done, Changed or Dropped, and the last phase (P8) cannot close while any row is still Open.

Status values:

- **Open**: not yet ported. This is the starting status of almost every row.
- **Done**: ported and checked against 0.90.34; the Note says where and how it was checked.
- **Changed**: 2.0 deliberately behaves differently, for a reason PLAN.md already decides (D1 run launching, D4 identifier, D5 defect fixes, D7 random seeds, SF Symbols drawn as lucide icons through a name table, UserDefaults stored as JSON files, SwiftTerm replaced by xterm.js). The reason is in the Note column.
- **Dropped**: not carried over, for a reason PLAN.md §4 gives (dead code, unused methods, unbundled programs). The reason is in the Note column.

This ledger was drafted on 2026-11-10 from the 0.90.34 sources at commit `dc066f0` (`2_QNET/Sources/Qnet`, 94 files), with `canvas.md`, `shell.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md` and `docs/gui_work/BACKLOG.json` used only to find things. Every row still Open must be re-checked against the source in the phase that ports it; a line number cited here can drift, and a row can be wrong.

Phases, from PLAN.md §7: P1 model and files; P2 exporters; P3 solver runtime, parser and results store; P4 workspace, menus, settings, file handling and Status log; P5 canvas and inspectors; P6 shell, run interface, results interface, Method Chooser, Network Model window, test sets and dependency check; P7 assistant, Help and About; P8 packaging and the parity gate.

## 1. Menus and shortcuts

The menu bar is `QnetCommands` (App, File, Edit, View, Network, Tools, Run, Test, Help) plus `WorkspaceCommands` (View ▸ Panes, Window items), both installed from `QnetGUIApp.body` `.commands { }`. Items marked "standard" are supplied by SwiftUI/AppKit rather than Qnet code; their exact set depends on the macOS version and is not determined from source.

## 2. Toolbar items

One customizable SwiftUI toolbar, `.toolbar(id: "qnet.main")`, on the main window (style `.unified`, default window 1500 × 900). All items are `.primaryAction` and, being in a customizable toolbar with no customization behaviour set, can be removed or rearranged in View ▸ Customize Toolbar…; macOS persists the arrangement by item id. Icons are SF Symbols and become lucide icons through the name table.

| ID | What 0.90.34 does | Where (source) | Phase | Status | Note |

## 3. Canvas

Everything drawn, hit-tested and edited on the network canvas, plus the canvas-hosted status bar and the menu items whose action needs the canvas. Constants were checked against the Swift source; where `canvas.md` and the source disagree the row follows the source and says so in Note.

## 4. Inspectors and parameter panels

The node and link inspectors exist in two hosts that render the same section views bound to the same draft objects: the docked Inspector pane, which commits each field on blur, and the movable "Node Parameters" / "Link Parameters" panels (⌘I), which commit on Save. There is no network-level inspector and no multi-node editing; the only network-wide field, the buffer mode, is edited from any buffer's inspector.

## 5. Workspace

The main window: document tabs over one stable split tree of seven panes (the canvas plus six switchable panes), detached pane windows, movable panels, file open/save, and session restore. Menu rows themselves are listed by another section; rows here record what the actions do.

## 6. Settings

AppSettings.swift declares 108 `@AppStorage` keys (96 named plus 3 per-provider families of 4); every one is in `AppSettings.defaultsByKey` and therefore in the export. Further keys are written outside AppSettings (Settings/Help window state, canvas export options, tab and shell persistence, split sizes, window frames) and one Keychain service holds the AI API keys. Reader citations are `File.swift:function`; "Settings binding" means the Settings window control itself.

## 7. Methods

Every Run-menu method, every composite run, and the run mechanics common to all of them. Paths under `bin/` are relative to `Qnet.app/Contents/Resources/` (or the same layout in the source tree). `<in>` is the exported temp input in `NSTemporaryDirectory`, `<pid>` the app's process id.

### 7.7 Run mechanics common to all methods

| ID | What 0.90.34 does | Where (source) | Phase | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RUN-001 | Solver roots are searched in this order: bundled `Contents/Resources/bin`; `QNET_SOLVER_ROOT` (as `.app/Contents/Resources/bin`, the root, `root/bin`, `root/Contents/Resources/bin`); a nearby `Qnet.app/Contents/Resources/bin` in up to 7 ancestors of the working directory and of the executable's directory; those same ancestors as a source tree. A packaged copy therefore beats a source-tree binary. | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift runtimeRoots | P3 | Changed | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs. The development tier is explicit (`development_roots`): the staged cache tree ~/Library/Caches/qnet/solvers/stage/Resources/bin, then the repository's solvers/ in debug builds only; 0.90.34 searched 7 ancestors of the working directory and of the executable because it built its solvers in place. The order bundle → QNET_SOLVER_ROOT → nearby Qnet.app → development tree holds. runner/tests/resolver.rs. |
| RUN-002 | Each root is tried as `<root>/<group>/<subdir>/<name>` for each group (default finite then infinite) and then `<root>/<subdir>/<name>`; duplicate candidates are removed. | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift candidates | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs and resolver/{engine,probe}.rs; runner/tests/resolver.rs. |
| RUN-003 | A native candidate must exist, be executable and pass the loadability probe; every attempt is recorded as not found, not executable ("the file exists but lacks execute permission"), dynamic loader rejected, runtime unavailable or selected. | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift resolveExecutable | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs and resolver/{engine,probe}.rs; runner/tests/resolver.rs. |
| RUN-004 | Loadability probe: the candidate is launched with `--qnet-loadability-probe`, stdin and stdout null, cwd its own directory, env `QNET_RUNTIME_PROBE=1`, 0.8 s timeout then terminate and SIGKILL after 0.2 s; stderr containing "library not loaded", "dyld:", "dyld[", "symbol not found", "dependent dylib", "code signature invalid", "mapped file has no cdhash", "bad cpu type in executable" or "exec format error" rejects it; any exit or reaching the timeout otherwise passes. | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift launchProbe, loaderFailureMessage | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs and resolver/{engine,probe}.rs; runner/tests/resolver.rs. |
| RUN-005 | Probe results are cached per path and reused while the file's size and modification time are unchanged (separate caches for native and Python probes). | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift cachedProbe, cachedPythonProbe | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs and resolver/{engine,probe}.rs; runner/tests/resolver.rs. |
| RUN-006 | Python support files are resolved like executables but need only be readable ("support file is readable"); then a Python runtime is attached. | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift resolveSupportFile, resolvePythonSupportFile | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs and resolver/{engine,probe}.rs; runner/tests/resolver.rs. |
| RUN-007 | python3 discovery: every `PATH` entry (empty entry = cwd), then `/usr/bin/python3`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/python3`, `/usr/local/bin/python3`, deduplicated and executable only; each is probed in turn until one imports all required modules. | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift executableCandidates, resolvePythonRuntime | P8 | Changed | Changed (ROADMAP A2, 2026-11-12): Qnet's own Python comes first so the Python solvers run on a Mac with no Python installed. A lookup for `python3` tries `<app>/Contents/Resources/python/bin/python3` (Resolver::bundled_python), then the development stage `$HOME/Library/Caches/qnet/python/stage/Resources/python/bin/python3` (Resolver::development_python, HOME from the injected environment; made by scripts/stage-python.sh), then 0.90.34's search (PATH entries, /usr/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin) unchanged as the fallback; any other interpreter name is searched as before. Probes, cache and sentences are 0.90.34's. runner/src/resolver.rs executable_candidates; runner/tests/resolver.rs “qnets_own_python_comes_before_the_users”, “a_bundled_python_that_fails_its_check_gives_way_to_the_users”, “only_python3_means_qnets_own_python”, “the_staged_runtime_works_as_a_bundled_one_with_no_python_installed”. |
| RUN-008 | Python probe runs `<python> -B -c "import importlib, sys; [importlib.import_module(name) for name in sys.argv[1:]]; print(...)" <modules>` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, 2.0 s timeout; failures report "Python preflight exited with status N: …", "Python preflight timed out after 2.00 seconds" or "Python runtime 'python3' was not found in PATH or a standard installation location". | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift launchPythonProbe, PythonRuntimeLookup | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs and resolver/{engine,probe}.rs; runner/tests/resolver.rs. |
| RUN-009 | Python solvers are always launched as `"<interpreter>" -B "<script>" …` with the probed interpreter so no bytecode is written into the signed bundle. | SolverRuntimeResolver.swift resolvePythonSupportFile; QnetGUIApp.swift resolveEngine | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/resolver.rs and resolver/{engine,probe}.rs; runner/tests/resolver.rs. PA 2026-11-12: the bundled `python3` is a /bin/sh launcher that starts `python3.15` beside it with `-E -s -B`, unsets PYTHONPATH, PYTHONHOME, PYTHONSTARTUP, PYTHONUSERBASE, PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX, PYTHONINSPECT and PYTHONSAFEPATH and exports PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 for any child Python. `-I` is not used because it also removes the script's own folder from the module path and the solvers import their neighbours. The runtime carries bytecode made at stage time as unchecked-hash .pyc (no timestamp, relative paths, never rewritten): without it importing NumPy takes 1.3 s instead of 0.1 s, against the 2 s probe. The signature still verifies after a solver run (measured on a trial bundle). |

## 8. Exporters and file formats

Rows cover the `.bnet` document, station ordering, every solver-input exporter and dialect, their refusal messages, the Export menu and headless export flags, and every other file the app reads or writes. FILE- rows are files that are not solver inputs; EXP- rows are solver inputs.

## 9. Result parser

`ResultOutputParser.parse` runs once per successful run, on the full captured output. It reads each line through the rules below in order, and the first rule that matches a line wins (`continue`). It then scans the whole text for evidence rows, and finally sets the disposition, where later checks override earlier ones.

| ID | What 0.90.34 does | Where (source) | Phase | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PARSE-001 | Nil or empty output gives no measurements, the warning "The solver completed without capturable standard output." and failure "The solver exited successfully but produced no output. No performance measures can be trusted from this run." | ResultOutputParser.swift `parse` | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/; core/tests/golden_results.rs re-parses all 490 golden records identically, and every launched golden run is filed and compared with its record.json (runner/tests/methods_*.rs). |
| PARSE-002 | Before matching, the text has ANSI CSI sequences (`ESC[…<final>`) removed, percent-delta annotations such as ` (+1.2%)` removed, and every CR replaced by LF. It is then split on LF, keeping empty lines. | ResultOutputParser.swift `normalized`, `ansi`, `percentDelta` | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/; core/tests/golden_results.rs re-parses all 490 golden records identically, and every launched golden run is filed and compared with its record.json (runner/tests/methods_*.rs). |

## 10. Analysis and diagnostics

Traffic equations, utilisation, the silent (live) analysis behind the flag bar, network warnings, link-structure rules, analytical tractability, SRBM existence and recurrence, the Analyze Network and Network Primitives reports, the Method Chooser, the Network Model window and the startup dependency check. Analyze Network and Show Network Primitives are not separate windows in 0.90.34: both reports are written to a temp file and `cat`-ed into the Interactive Shell.

### 10.1 Traffic equations and utilisation

### 11.4 How runs are recorded

| ID | What 0.90.34 does | Where (source) | Phase | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RES-043 | A record is registered when a run is launched: its id is the run handle's id, it is keyed to the tab that was active at launch (tab id and title), it takes a snapshot of that tab's network with the run's parameters, seed and replication seeds, it is inserted at the top with status running, and the notification `qnetResultRunDidBegin` is posted with tabID and runID. | QnetGUIApp.swift `runScript`, `registerStructuredResult`; ResultsWorkspace.swift `beginRun` | P6 | Changed | D1: no qnetResultRunDidBegin notification. The record is filed at launch by src-tauri/src/runs.rs start (tab id and title, snapshot, parameters, seeds, status running, at the top) and announced as results://changed with the tab id, which refreshes useResults; the Results pane shows it running (ResultsPane.test.tsx “waits for its measurements with a spinner…”). The one listener of the notification, the first-run reveal, follows onRunFinished (WS-016). |
| RES-044 | When a run finishes: a cancelled run's record is deleted; a non-zero exit is recorded as failed with "<label> exited with status N. See the originating tab's Status pane and retained output."; a successful exit is parsed and recorded as completed, partial or failed with the parser's message. The full transcript is stored as rawOutput in every case. | QnetGUIApp.swift `finalizeStructuredResult` | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/ and runner/src/store.rs; core/tests/golden_results.rs (490 of 490 records) and runner/tests/store.rs. |
| RES-045 | Records finish through the terminal model's last-run summary; the record is matched by run id, so a late completion is never attached to the wrong tab. | QnetGUIApp.swift `.onChange(of: terminalModel.lastRunSummary)` | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: runner/src/store.rs; runner/tests/store.rs, and every golden run filed through it. |
| RES-046 | A run whose output has no recognised station measurements is recorded as failed ("The solver produced no recognized station performance measures."), except that BAR Moment Bounds uses its own SDP-backend message. | ResultOutputParser.swift `parse` (measurements.isEmpty) | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/ and runner/src/store.rs; core/tests/golden_results.rs (490 of 490 records) and runner/tests/store.rs. |
| RES-047 | Test Set (`testset`) and Spectral Convergence (`spc`) runs are always recorded as failed, because their aggregate error tables contain no station rows the parser recognises. | QnetGUIApp.swift `finalizeStructuredResult`; ResultOutputParser.swift `parse`; QnetGUIApp.swift `runScript(label: "testset" / "spc")` | P3 | Changed | D5: fixed in 2.0; these runs must record as completed with their aggregate results. P3 2026-11-11: built as described (core/src/results/, runner/src/store.rs; runner/tests/store.rs). |
| RES-048 | Partial results are recorded for: adaptive BAR not converged, regenerative MC precision target not met, adaptive MLMC sample cap hit, truncated CTMC not converged, SBD fallback used, and a comparison with failed or skipped methods. Regenerative MC with zero cycles is recorded as failed. | ResultOutputParser.swift `parse` disposition rules | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/ and runner/src/store.rs; core/tests/golden_results.rs (490 of 490 records) and runner/tests/store.rs. |
| RES-049 | Comparison runs get the warning "The structured table records the first value in each comparison row; the retained raw output contains every method column." | ResultOutputParser.swift `parse` | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/ and runner/src/store.rs; core/tests/golden_results.rs (490 of 490 records) and runner/tests/store.rs. |
| RES-050 | A record is stale when its fingerprint differs from the fingerprint of the current canvas of the tab being viewed. | ResultsWorkspace.swift `ResultRunRecord.isStale` | P3 | Changed | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/ and runner/src/store.rs; core/tests/golden_results.rs (490 of 490 records) and runner/tests/store.rs. Changed in 2.1 (2026-11-12): a run is also current when the network differs from the one it was made from only in layout (node positions and pictures). 0.90.34 compared fingerprints, which cover positions, so tidying a diagram marked every result stale. The stored fingerprint is unchanged (src/results/current.ts sameNetwork, structureKey; current.test.ts). |
| RES-051 | The "previous comparable run" is the most recent older completed record in the same tab with the same method identifier and the same fingerprint. | ResultsWorkspace.swift `previousComparableRun(for:)` | P6 | Done | model.ts previousComparableRun (model.test.ts “is the latest older completed run of the same method and network snapshot”). |
| RES-052 | The Results pane shows only the records whose provenance.tabID equals the active tab's id. | ResultsWorkspace.swift `records(for:)`, `tabRecords` | P3 | Done | P3 2026-11-11: core/src/results/ and runner/src/store.rs; core/tests/golden_results.rs (490 of 490 records) and runner/tests/store.rs. |
| RES-053 | Because records are keyed to the tab id, they disappear from view when the tab is reopened (Reopen Closed Tab gives a new id), when tabs are not restored at relaunch, or when the same file is opened in a new tab; the records stay on disk with no way to see them. | ResultsWorkspace.swift `records(for:)`; TabClosing.swift `ClosedTab.makeTab` | P6 | Changed | D5 fixed: the reopened tab keeps its id (WS-048) and the restored session keeps every tab's id (WS-136), so their records show again. Records stay keyed to the tab id (RES-052); a file opened afresh in another tab starts its own list, as in 0.90.34. |

## 12. Shell pane

The Shell pane is a real login shell in a pseudo-terminal, drawn by the vendored SwiftTerm 1.13.0. Under D1 the app no longer types solver runs into it; runs are started by the Rust supervisor and their output is shown in the pane.

### 12.1 Process, environment and lifetime

| ID | What 0.90.34 does | Where (source) | Phase | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SH-001 | The pane runs the user's login shell, read from the password database with `getpwuid_r`; if that lookup fails it falls back to `/bin/zsh`. | TerminalConsoleView.swift `TerminalHostView.userShell()`; shell.md §3.1 | P6 | Done | src-tauri/src/shell/pty.rs user_shell(): getpwuid_r's pw_shell, /bin/zsh when the lookup fails; shell.rs test the_login_shell_is_started_with_a_dash. ## 13. AI assistant

The AI Assistant pane is a per-tab chat with an LLM that can read and edit the tab's network and run solvers through nine tools. Requests leave from Rust in 2.0; that is a change of mechanism only, so the provider rows stay Open.

## 15. Headless CLI flags

`handleCLIIfNeeded` runs in `QnetGUIApp.init` before any window; it inspects `argv[1]` only (except `--ds-gallery`, `--loss-fix`, `--bas-fix`). All output goes to stdout except the settings audit.

### 17.2 Index of known defects fixed on purpose (D5)

Each defect in PLAN §5 has a Changed row where the behaviour lives. This list only points to them; it adds no rows.

- Product-form solver shipped without `mva.py`: METH-030, PKG-021.
- Test Set and Spectral Convergence runs always recorded as failed: METH-150, RES-047, TEST-019, TEST-029.
- Result records orphaned when a tab is reopened: WS-048, RES-053.
- The link menu's class picker can create a duplicate link: CAN-144.
- The one-station "general P-matrix" random network has a routing row that does not sum to 1: GEN-022.
- AI: an unmatched tool call left in history after a cancel: AI-037. `max_tokens` stops never shown: AI-026.
- `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` describes SuiteSparse as LGPL and Apache: PKG-019, ABOUT-005.
- Not in PLAN §5 but fixed in P0 the same way: the BNAsm deployment target, PKG-020.
